subject: Post-call recap: cost anchors, batching levers & ops asks
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@paywise.com>, PayWise Ops <ops@paywise.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: cost anchors, batching levers & ops asks

Sara / PayWise team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while items are fresh and a proposed next set of asks so we can model an apples-to-apples TCO for the pilot.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Token cost exposure on high-volume invoice parsing (esp. peak EOD loads).
- Latency constraints for synchronous customer-facing validation (~250ms P95 target).
- Procurement wants a straightforward TCO and a clear failure/fallback plan before infra sign-off.

Goals we aligned on:
1) Reduce per-transaction inference cost to fit your budget envelope (~$0.03/transaction target for the use-case).
2) Keep user-facing latency under 250ms P95 for the majority of flows; allow async for bulk reconciliations.
3) Pilot runway: 3 months with a success metric of 30% reduction in manual review rates.

Initial cost levers we discussed (for modeling):
- Batch windowing for non-real-time flows (expected 2–5x token throughput on batch-friendly endpoints).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated vendor templates (estimated 10–20% token savings).
- Quantized model variant for the majority of calls, with a small set routed to the higher-accuracy model.

Next operational asks from PayWise (per call):
- Ops: sample traffic profile (hour-by-hour request counts) and a representative prompt set.
- Procurement: contract timeline and standard redlines (we can provide a minimal SOW + subscription terms).
- Product: top 10 transaction examples we should add to the eval set.

I attached a first-pass TCO workbook and draft SOW to help frame options. Ben will follow up with a short note on latency tradeoffs and a simplified pilot configuration (minimum footprint + burst plan).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Today (Fri): Evelyn shares TCO workbook + draft SOW (attached).
- Mon (May 10): PayWise sends traffic profile + sample prompts.
- Tue (May 11): 30-min tech sync between PayWise infra and Ben to validate latency assumptions.

If this aligns, can you confirm the Mon/Tue cadence and who from Ops will own the traffic sample?

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Sara / team — quick note ahead of Tue's tech sync. I pulled a couple of simple slices into the attached TCO workbook and added a "fast-estimate" tab to illustrate sensitivity to three levers: batching window, cache hit-rate, and model variant split. Highlights: 

- Baseline per-transaction token estimate: 420 tokens/request (avg).
- With 2s micro-batching for non-blocking flows, effective tokens/tokenization overhead drops ~1.6x at 95th percentile of batchable traffic.
- Prefix caching at 30% hit rate yields ~12% cost reduction on the token bill (conservative).
- Quantized model option (8-bit) shows latency improvement of ~25ms median on our internal benchmarks with an observed ~1–2% F1 drop on vendor field extraction tests.

Attached: redwood_tco_model.xlsx (fast-estimate tab). I also included three pilot configs for your procurement review:
A) Minimal footprint (single dedicated pool, quantized primary) — lowest cost, higher routing to full model on edge cases.
B) Balanced (dedicated + burst, split routing 80/20) — balance of latency and accuracy.
C) Accuracy-first (larger footprint, smaller quantized share) — more expensive but lower regression risk.

For Tue: I'll bring an ops-level diagram showing fallback routing and a short SLO matrix. Priyom will join to cover quota/commit sizing and to outline a simple canary rollout pattern.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
